rows.description: I wonder if the fighting is because of me, my marks or my mess. Children often blame themselves, but adult problems are not caused by kids. If I ask, a parent should tell me clearly it is not my fault.

rows.description: I am angry at both of them for ruining our home. Anger covers sadness. Wise: say it in words, maybe draw or run. Slamming doors is natural, but hurting others or blaming one parent unfairly will hurt me more.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comfort, fear, grief, guilt, hope, loyalty
related mind states: sadness, anger, hurt

rows.description: Each parent says bad things about the other, and I feel torn. I love both. A wise child says I do not want to be in the middle. Being a messenger or spy for either parent is too heavy for me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, fear, grief, guilt, hope
related mind states: affection

rows.description: When my parents separate, I miss the old family and cry at odd times. Grief is normal even though nobody died. I keep routines, talk about it, and let myself be sad without hurrying to be okay.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, fear, guilt, hope, loyalty
related mind states: sadness, grief

rows.description: I keep hoping they will get back together and imagine plans to fix it. This is common, but I cannot fix their marriage. Accepting slowly frees me to enjoy time with each parent as it is.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, fear, grief, guilt, loyalty
related mind states: hope

rows.description: As a parent I explain calmly that the split is not the child's fault and that we both love them. Wise parents avoid badmouthing the other and keep routines. Using a child as a confidant or messenger harms them.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, grief, guilt, hope, loyalty
related mind states: affection, calm

rows.description: My grandmother holds me and says the house may change but her love will not. Being with a steady elder calms me. Family in India often carries this role well; I accept the warmth and speak honestly.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, grief, guilt, hope, loyalty

rows.description: I do not want friends to know about the separation, and I feel ashamed. Many families go through it. I choose one trusted friend to tell. Hiding it forever costs more than sharing with someone kind.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, fear, grief, guilt, hope
related mind states: shame, embarrassment, trust

rows.description: One parent bribes me with gifts and hints I should choose them. It feels nice but wrong. I can say I love you both and do not want to choose. A child should never be a prize in an adult dispute.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, fear, grief, guilt, hope
related mind states: affection

rows.description: After the separation the house is quieter and I feel relieved, then guilty for feeling that. Both feelings are true. Relief from tension is not betrayal, and I can miss them and feel calmer at once.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, comfort, fear, grief, guilt, hope
